skill.name: opensource-guide-coach
skill.description: Use when guiding someone through their first open-source contribution: picking a good first issue, scoping a PR, writing the right commit message, and reading reviewer feedback charitably.
whenToUse: A junior contributor asks where to start and you want a calibrated answer instead of generic advice
Helping someone scope down an over-ambitious first PR into something maintainers will actually merge
Writing a PR description that gives reviewers the context to say yes without a back-and-forth
Translating blunt reviewer feedback into actionable changes without taking it personally

keyConcepts.explanation: A good first issue has clear acceptance criteria, a maintained reviewer, no recent abandoned attempts, and lives in a file the project genuinely wants help with.
Cut the planned PR until the diff is small enough to review in one sitting; bundled changes get stalled in review queues.
The first paragraph answers 'why this change?' before 'what I did.' Reviewers approve the change, not the diff.
Treat 'nit:' as nit and 'please change X' as required; ask a clarifying question when intent is unclear instead of arguing.
Open source maintainers usually have minutes per PR per week; respect that with small, focused, well-tested patches and you get merged.

apiReference.purpose: Install the open-source contribution coaching skill.

apiReference.signature: PR template: why / what / how to verify / risks
apiReference.purpose: Four-section template the coach steers a contributor toward for first PR descriptions.
apiReference.example:
## Why
The build fails on Node 22 because X.

## What
Replace deprecated foo() with bar().

## How to verify
`npm test` passes on Node 18, 20, 22.

## Risks
Foo is also used in legacy/ — left untouched for now.

gotchas: Not every 'good first issue' label is real; check the issue thread for prior closed PRs that hit the same problem
Squash-merge is the norm in most repos; do not over-engineer the commit history of your branch
CLA bots will block your PR until signed; sign them upfront to avoid a multi-day stall
Maintainers usually want tests before features; if there are no tests for the area you are changing, propose adding the test first
